column1: # One note per line: id, points, text, then key=value fields, split by tabs. Format: https://teoyujie.org/api/notes.txt

column3: I predict one of the surprises, to some people anyway, is going to be that autonomous vehicles don't clog city streets.
If there is a task with enough value to automate, a specialized robot will win that market.
I would bet against the imminent commodification of autonomous vehicle technology.
Effectively every single H100 in existence now will be e-waste in 5 years or less.
Selling the output of a LLM is going to an incredibly cut-throat and low-margin business.
I think SWE headcounts will reduce over time.
as model capabilities plateau (I'm not an accelerationist) the harnesses and products around them will start to specialize.
The 128 GB Mac Studio is no longer sold and when they bring it back I predict it will be more expensive.
I think it will split between TSMC (sold out forever) and Samsung/Intel (please please be our customer).
I would bet that AIs will master taste and human psychology before they'll cure cancer.
in two years time Waymo will probably be available to the majority of the US population.
We might have 600MW of SMR's within a decade, but we're highly unlikely to have 6GW.
I'll believe in three years we'll be able to run ~30B models on the best phones.
in the end I suspect efficiency will be the winning feature.
If I could bet on this, I would bet everything I could on "skill with LLMs" being the high order bit of being an effective software developer 5 years from now.
They've all avoided loading up their LLMs with ads to this point. That is going to change dramatically over the next 2-3 years.
Half of PayPal's business goes away over the coming decade.
these computing price increases will be what finally makes certain ML startups un-economical.
I think the Internet will, sometime in the near future, just get shut down.
I won’t be surprised if my kid looks back on Anthropic and OpenAI the way we look back on Sun and Netscape.
It seems very very unlikely that an Opus 5 matching local model that runs on a 5070 will be released within the next 5 years.
I think Anthropic and OpenAI's margins will erode some over time.
The cuts will have arrived by 2030, but the bill will be old news.
I expect AIs to pass the human baseline here by the end of the year. (On the benchmark Radiology's Last Exam 2.0.)
I expect robust demand for cybersecurity and other defenses within a year's time, regardless of whether that transition goes smoothly.
The sl4.org website will be gone by 2030 at the latest.
Nick Szabo, Hal Finney, Wei Dai and other named candidates are not Satoshi, settled by 2030.
Powerful LLMs will be deployed at global scale in the next few years, and will dominate the Internet, and increasingly, ordinary life.
Kurzweil's 2019 predictions mostly true by 2029 (15%), by 2039 (25%).
Fifty percent chance the AI point of no return happens by 2030.
I think Taiwan invasion is very plausible but I wouldn't say it's likely by 2030 even assuming superhuman coders. Maybe 50/50?
By the end of 2026, there will be an AI system accessible to members of the public like me, that can build its own scaffold for a typical turn-based video game.
It's possible that there'll be an AI funding winter in the next few years but we don't think there will be.
94%: no AGI doing nearly every economically valuable task cheaper than humans by 2030.
97%: no language model writes a New York Times bestseller without substantial aid by 2030.
I put the probability that AI will directly cause humanity to go extinct within the next 30 years at roughly 4%.
I predict that forming deep social bonds with AIs will become normalized.
AGI will not arrive before 2030 (60%) but will before 2060 (67%).
By 2030 language systems can be made to almost never pose as human.
The METR trend in AI task length is more likely to slow down by 2027 than to speed up, relative to the 2024-2025 trend.
Mass-market flying cars will not arrive before mid-century, probably not this century.
Online discussion norms may break down by 2026-2036 as manipulative AI participants outnumber humans.
Transformative AI (economy doubling every 4 years) by 2040, about 25%.
I think ARC has a ~10% chance of achieving our most ambitious goals before broadly superhuman AI obsoletes our labor.
Delaying uncontrollable AI by 4 years would be very challenging, and I think it's less likely than not.
75 percent chance over 1000 people live on seasteads by 2030.
15%: noisy intermediate-scale quantum computers solve a useful problem or become viable by 2030.
Over 70% chance of a Rubik's Cube-solving, chopsticks-using robotic hand by 2030.
70%: by 2030 shoppers no longer give merchants reusable credit card numbers.
Within 20 years of 2015 a computer finds a major mathematical conjecture without human help.
About 1 percent chance of a Singularity-type event within 40 years of 2011.
I predict we won't run out of compute or credit, though prices may rise a fair bit, and that will cause some companies to fail.
99 percent probability that AI is developed by 2070.
